sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
**RESCUE (2026-09-12):** the prior framework-only draft was an artifact of a network-availability error
(Medco IR site reported unreachable). Primary sources ARE reachable this session; all load-bearing
parameters below are now filled and cited to filed figures. No price, flow, or market-implied number has
been viewed. Phase 2 fills entry/exit/valuation-on-share levels from this committed base.

**Model** — upstream E&P producer valued at through-cycle NAV (VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL), not spot
earnings, plus a DCF-on-contracted-cashflows component for Medco Power (dividend_income_anchor
cross-anchor, rate 0.60).

### 1. Production × realized price = revenue (all AR2025)
- **Total annual production 2025: 156.1 mboepd** [AR2025 p.38 production-by-asset table: total Oil & Gas
  Production 156.1; = 147.1 mboepd conventional + 9.0 engineering/service Oman]; Oil/Gas split **28% oil /
  72% gas** [AR2025 p.58 "average production was 156 mboepd, comprising 72% gas and 28% oil"]. 2026 guidance
  **165–170 mboepd** [AR2025 p.19].
- **Realized oil price: US$66.6/bbl (2025)** (2024: $78.0) [AR2025 p.75 Operational Highlights: Average Oil
  Price]. **Realized gas price: US$6.8/mmbtu (2025)** (2024: $7.0) [AR2025 p.75 Average Gas Price].
- Revenue: **Total revenues FY2025 US$2,395.0M** (2024: $2,399.2M) [AR2025 p.172 income statement / p.74
  highlights]; Oil&gas-sales contracts $2,189.5M, electricity-power contracts $73.8M [AR2025 p.368 Note 34].
  Structural thesis holds: gas-weighted (72%) mix sells into a structurally short domestic gas market; half
  of gas production is under long-term fixed-price contracts (de-risks oil-price volatility) [AR2025 p.113].

### 2. Cash margin / cost-curve quartile
- **Consolidated lifting cost ≈ US$8.3/boe** — derived: Production & lifting costs $470.5M [AR2025 p.172]
  / 57.0 mmboe/yr production (156.1 mboepd × 365). Sub-US$10 lifting cost places MEDC in the **bottom cost
  curve quartile** among Indonesian E&P (favorable, PSC cost-recovery economics; E&P gross margin 55%:
  E&P gross profit $837.0M / E&P external sales $1,525.5M [AR2025 p.409 Note 44]).

### 3. FCF = OCF − (upstream capex + Medco Power capex)
- **Operating cash flow FY2025: US$906.3M** (2024: $1,219.5M) [MEDC_FY25.pdf p.26 cash flow: net cash
  provided by operating activities]. Revenue → OCF conversion = 906.3/2,395.0 ≈ **38%**.
- **Capex split FY2025 (balance-sheet): Oil & Gas US$402.1M; Power US$60.5M; Total US$462.6M** [AR2025
  p.28 Capital Expenditure table]. (Segment basis: E&P $411.5M, Services $83.2M, Power $23.8M, total
  $518.8M [AR2025 p.410 Note 44].) Note FY25 also carried one-off $355.0M business acquisition + $91.3M
  financial-asset placement in investing [MEDC_FY25 p.26] — non-recurring.
- **EBITDA FY2025: US$1,264.0M** (2024: $1,271.8M) [AR2025 p.74]. Operator capex coverage is strong:
  906.3 OCF vs 462.6 balance-sheet capex (≈2.0x cover).

### 4. Leverage / FCF-at-trough-Brent (kill-critical sensitivity)
- **Gross debt FY2025: US$3,646M** (2024: $3,300M) [AR2025 p.26/p.28]; cash $569.1M + restricted $59.8M
  [AR2025 p.74]. **Net debt ≈ US$3.0B**; **net debt-to-EBITDA ≈ 2.0x (management views)** (2024: 1.8x),
  "within our targeted" range [AR2025 p.26]. Net Debt/Equity 1.28x [AR2025 p.74].
- **Through-cycle Brent where upstream FCF turns negative: ≈ US$45/bbl (analyst estimate, derived — not a
  filed line).** Constructed from filed figures: at realized $66.6 oil / $6.8 gas the E&P segment gross
  margin is 55% and lifting cost $8.3/boe; OCF ≥ 2x organic capex. Sustained Brent far below the ~$66.6
  realized level — roughly halving O&G realisations — would be required to push upstream FCF negative,
  implying a ~$45 Brent through-cycle breakeven, comfortably below the ~104 Brent war-premium macro frame
  and the $74–85 range the prior idea card tested. Method stated; treat as the falsification input, not a
  guarantee. Management confirms low-price resilience: "sustained low oil prices → cost optimisation,
  reductions in production costs and adjustments to capex/exploration" [AR2025 p.113].

### 5. Reserve base
- **2P reserves 2025: 563.8 mmboe** (2P oil 123.5 + 2P gas 2,387.5 bcf); 2024: 493.4 mmboe → **reserve
  replacement > 1.0 confirmed FY25** (+14% y/y); 1P total 385.7 mmboe; contingent resources 1,153.9 mmboe
  [AR2025 p.75 / p.25]. 
- **Reserve life = 2P/production ≈ 9.9 years** (derived 563.8/57.0); AR states **2P Reserve Life Index 11.4
  years** (composite incl. service/Oman) [AR2025 p.25/p.35].
- **Block A (Aceh), 85% interest — net production 5.2 mboepd (2025)** [AR2025 p.38/p.41]; **decline**:
  6.8 (2024) → 5.2 (2025) = **−24% y/y**; from 8.4 peak (2022) -38% over 3y; gas 32.8→25.1 mmscfd (−23% y/y)
  [AR2025 p.38/39]. Block A is being actively sustained — 20-year PSC extension proposed Dec 2025, Phase 2
  development to hold gas commitments [AR2025 p.41]. Offset by South Natuna Block B growth: 13.2→19.6 mboepd
  (+49%, Terubuk/Forel start-up) and Block 60 Oman 12.6→13.6 mboepd [AR2025 p.38]. Reserve growth (564 vs
  493) confirms replacement > 1.0 this year; the make-or-break is whether 2026-27 (full Corridor 24%+
  Terubuk+Forel, guidance 165-170) offsets Block A runoff — 2026 guidance is 5.6-8.9% above 2025 actuals.

### Cross-anchor (Medco Power, contracted floor)
- **Installed operating IPP capacity: 1,011 MW** (15 IPPs operating + 100 MW development; gas-fired ELB
  109MW, Medco Ratch Riau 275MW, geothermal Sarulla 330MW/Ijen 35MW, solar PV, mini-hydro) [AR2025 p.49].
- **Power segment external revenue FY2025: US$177.6M** [AR2025 p.409 Note 44]; electricity-power contract
  revenue $73.8M + power lease/finance income on concession assets $10.9M [AR2025 p.368 Note 34]; power
  sales 4,371 GWh (+6% y/y, 25% renewables), 2026 guide ~4,550 GWh [AR2025 p.47/17]. Power capex $60.5M
  (2025) vs $141.5M (2024) — the power buildout is past peak capex, releasing cash [AR2025 p.28]. This
  contracted, de-risked flow is the dividend_income_anchor analog (rate 0.60).

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** MEDC's upside is capped — a mature/declining upstream, a capital-hungry power buildout,
and high-cost consolidated production mean it mostly pays a covered dividend rather than re-rate on the
commodity cycle.
**Why wrong:** As an upstream producer it is a *long* Brent war-premium (realized prices rise with ~104),
not an oil-import loser; gas-weighted (72%) production sells into a structurally short domestic market at
oil-indexed prices, half under fixed-price contracts; E&P gross margin is 55% and lifting cost $8.3/boe —
bottom-quartile cost curve, not high-cost; reserve replacement is >1.0 (2P 564 vs 493 mmboe); and Medco
Power's contracted revenue (a 1,011 MW IPP base, past peak capex) is a volatility-reducing floor that
underwrites the through-cycle NAV — the market anchors it to dividend capacity (base-up) and misprices the
capex-cycle turnaround (base-up to through-cycle NAV). FY25 net profit of only $100.9M (dragged by $128.8M
impairments + $355M one-off acquisition) reads as weakness but cash generation (OCF $906M) is intact.
**What proves us wrong:** a 2P statement showing reserve replacement < 1.0 (Block A runoff), consolidated
cost curve above the 2nd quartile with upstream FCF negative inside a ~$45-104 Brent range, or Medco Power
contracted EBITDA not servicing net debt — each is now quantified above and the fy25 evidence argues the
opposite (replacement 1.14x, lifting $8.3/boe, net debt/EBITDA 2.0x).

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown:
It is three years forward and this position lost 30%. The most likely reason is that MEDC was a high-cost,
declining-reserve producer all along: the 2P statement showed reserve replacement < 1.0 at Block A, the
through-cycle Brent breakeven sat above the war-premium band once the geopolitics overlay repriced, and
Medco Power's contracted EBITDA did not actually delever the consolidated balance sheet — so the "contracted
floor" and "capex turnaround" both failed and the name re-rated down with the complex, not up with it. I
sized a commodity producer on a war premium instead of a sourced through-cycle price. The rescue data
softens but does not retire this risk: Block A IS declining (-24% y/y) and its attrition must be beaten by
South Natuna Block B, Corridor full-year and Block 60 growth to keep replacement above 1.0; if the 2026
165-170 mboepd guide (and the ~45 Brent FCF breakeven) both hold, the downside case needs a real reserve/price
double miss.

sections.heading: Bear attack
sections.markdown:
**Drew (BEAR) — VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL attack on T-INDO-MEDC-001**

1. **The "$45 Brent through-cycle FCF breakeven" is a derived guess, not a filed line** — extrapolated from one year's 55% margin and $8.3/boe lifting cost. Every historical downcycle hits realized prices faster than cost cuts, and your gas is 72% of boe. Halving realisations needs only ~35% below the ~104 war-premium; your own regime trips below ~81.5. Stress the breakeven against the 2020 trough before trusting it.

2. **Reserve replacement >1.0 is the wrong test; the 2026-27 2P statement is, and evidence already argues runoff.** Block A fell -24% y/y (-38% over 3y) to ~3% of production; Block B's +49% was start-up flush. Replacement was carried by undeveloped and contingent additions. If 2027 shows replacement <1.0 ex-Block-A, the thesis dies — your 2027-09-30 date-kill is 12 months out, too slow to protect capital.

3. **The "contracted floor" is mislabeled: half your gas is under fixed price, which caps BOTH directions.** You claim the ~104 Brent war-premium re-rate AND the fixed-price hedge. They contradict: fixed-price slugs simply won't re-rate with Brent, and if you're hedged to the jaw you're a slow lagging half-position, not the war-premium winner. Declare which leg carries the return — the floor or the re-rate — you cannot book both.

4. **Leverage is rising into the turn, not deleveraging:** net debt $3.0-3.6B while OCF fell 26% ($1,219M→$906M), and $355M acquisition + $128.8M impairment one-offs flattered the year. Power revenue ($177.6M) is ~6% of consolidated — that "floor" alone cannot service $3.6B gross debt. The $45-Brent downside you hand-wave away is exactly what trips the 2.5x net-debt/EBITDA gauge you set yourself.

5. **The up/down ratio is an archetype artifact, not MEDC-specific:** +75/-35 and 0.42 loaded from the registry, zero bottom-up NAV math — no PDP NAV/share, no Power multiple, no target. A 2.14 ratio and +43 Kelly from a registry prior applied to a -24% declining core asset is false precision that would let you size on nulls. Rebuild the valuation before any sizing; up-down ratios on the back of thin air aren't sizing inputs.

**Verdict: MAJOR_REVISION**
The $45 breakeven and reserve-replacement verdicts are both unfalsified this session, but the fixed-price-gas-vs-war-premium contradiction and the rising lever into declining Block A demand that the valuation be rebuilt before any sizing — the thesis cannot justify Kelly +43 on a null valuation.

sections.heading: Revision
sections.markdown:
1. **$45 breakeven acknowledged as derived, not filed.** Drew is correct: extrapolated from one year's 55% margin and $8.3/boe. The 2020 trough (realized ~$35-40) would have compressed margins further. Treat this as a working estimate with real uncertainty — the $45 figure is more a floor-of-confidence than a hard floor. Conservative posture: widen down_pct to reflect the unfalsified tail, not defend the number.

2. **2027 2P statement is the real test.** Reserve replacement >1.0 confirmed FY25 (493→564 mmboe), but Drew is right that Block B's +49% was startup flush and Block A IS in structural decline (-24% y/y, -38% from peak). The 9.9y RLI is a trailing metric. Kill date 2027-09-30 is indeed 12 months late for a capital-protecting signal. Add a Q1 2026 interim checkpoint: if 1Q26 production misses the 165-170 mboepd guide, update the replacement trajectory before FY annual filings land.

3. **Fixed-price contracts cap the war-premium re-rate.** Drew's contradiction stands: half the gas is fixed-price — it does NOT re-rate with Brent. The thesis must declare one leg: the fixed-price half is the floor (downside protection), not the upside. The Brent-re-rate play applies only to the spot-indexed 50% and the oil 28%. Overweighting the war-premium narrative overstates the re-rating leverage; correct the variant perception to reflect only half the portfolio participates.

4. **Leverage concern valid; Power floor is thin.** OCF fell 26% ($1,219M→$906M) — a real trend, not a one-off. Power revenue $177.6M against gross debt $3,646M confirms Drew: ~6% of revenue cannot service debt. The "contracted floor" is a cash-flow stability story, not a deleveraging engine. Net debt/EBITDA 2.0x is within target today, but the trajectory matters more than the snapshot — monitor quarterly OCF/capex coverage ratio.

5. **Kelly +43 is archetype-derived, not MEDC-specific NAV.** Drew is correct: no PDP NAV/share, no power DCF multiple, no through-cycle target. The +75/-35 and Kelly are loaded from the commodity_capex_turnaround registry prior applied to a specific name without bottom-up validation. Phase 2 must build the NAV before sizing. Do not treat the archetype ratio as a sizing input until the valuation is rebuilt from first principles.

sections.heading: Judge verdict
sections.markdown:
**Verdict: PASS_REDUCED 0.60**

**Grounds:**
1. **No null valuation — rate reduced.** The thesis carries no NAV/share, no power DCF multiple, no through-cycle price target. The +75/-35 up/down, Kelly +43, and expected +10.7% are archetype artifacts applied to a specific name without bottom-up anchor. Phase 2 must rebuild from PDP NAV and a power-segment DCF before sizing. Rate 0.60 (vs registry 0.42) reflects this gap — the archetype prior is too generous without named-specific valuation discipline.

2. **Reserve replacement is live, not settled.** FY25 2P rose 493→564 mmboe (+14%, rr>1.0). But Block A is in structural decline (-24% y/y, -38% from peak), Block B's +49% was start-up flush, and the 2026-27 2P statement is the real test. The Q1 2026 production checkpoint Drew forced is correct. The 2027-09-30 kill date is 12 months too slow; the interim gate partially closes that gap.

3. **Fixed-price floor is real but one-directional.** Half the gas is fixed-price — a downside buffer, not a war-premium re-rate lever. The revision correctly narrows the upside claim to the spot-indexed 50% gas and 28% oil only. The contracted-floor argument survives; the re-rating-leverage argument does not. This is an honest, narrower thesis — a net positive.

4. **Leverage trajectory is the single most live monitor.** OCF fell 26% ($1,219M→$906M) — a real trend. Net debt/EBITDA 2.0x is within target today, but direction matters. Power revenue ($177.6M against $3.6B gross debt) is a stability floor, not a deleveraging engine. OCF/capex coverage ratio is the right quarterly signal.

5. **Source integrity is solid.** Big-4 auditor, unqualified opinion, PP&E at cost (no revaluation distortion), OCF 9x net profit (clean conversion), reserve replacement confirmed FY25. The rescue fixed the network-availability artifact. Sources are auditable and internally consistent.

sections.markdown:
Both VETO hard gates are remediated: `data/dossiers/MEDC.fund record` now exists and `the market-cap feed` carries a
MEDC.JK record (mcap ~IDR 34.0T). Levels are read off the model, not a chosen band. Entry **1,400 IDR**
is a value-anchored limit ~7.6% below the 1,515 close: at spot the honest EV is a thin **+7.0%**
(0.42·48.5 − 0.58·39.3 + 9.9 − 0.5), so the limit is set at a margin-of-safety discount where base NAV
(2,250) still leaves +60.7% and bear NAV (920) a survivable −34.3% — restoring EV to **+15.0%**. Target
**2,250** = base NAV/share (through-cycle SOTP); kill **920** = bear NAV/share (~$45 Brent through-cycle,
upstream FCF ~0) — the falsification level, not a stop. ADV ~IDR 80B/day supports a 20%-participation exit
in a few sessions; ARA/ARB bands are not binding at this liquidity. Flows feed STALE — no flow narrative
underwritten.

sections.heading: Risk review
sections.markdown:
Layer 1 — `the risk checker --book INDO`: book compliant (NAV IDR 15,229,940,237.54, cash 100%, governor NONE,
week_trades 0). The 2026-09-16 VETO's two hard gates are re-verified remediated by direct call, not taken on
report:
- dossier gate — `_dossier_frozen("MEDC.JK")` = **False**; `data/dossiers/MEDC.fund record` present,
  `fundamentals_complete: true`, `asof: 2026-10-16` (fresh, ≤60d).
- market-cap gate — `market_cap("MEDC.JK","INDO")` = **IDR 33,999,536,551,750** (asof 2026-10-05,
  yfinance.fast_info), **> floor IDR 1,000,000,000,000**. the market-cap feed schema_version 1, generated 2026-10-05

Both PASS. No VETO.

Layer 2 (numbers):
1. **Factor tags** — the INDO universe `MEDC.JK`: factor=`oil_gas`, factor2=`energy`, sector=ENERGY. Both
   tags ∈ closed `factor_taxonomy`. Buyable.
2. **Stress-table honesty** — worst per-factor stress move = **-7.0%** (oil_gas; energy -6.0). At the binding
   PM cap **6.00% NAV**: post-trade **stress-day book loss = 0.42% NAV (IDR 63,965,749)**. Governor headroom
   from dd 0.0%: **7.58pp to -8% REVIEW / 14.58pp to -15% DEGROSS**. Book heat after 0.42% ≪ 12.0% budget.
3. **Concentration in disguise** — single-name, empty book: no live overlap today. Flag: the position is
   counted under **both** `oil_gas` and `energy` (factor ruler double-counts the same underlying Brent/gas
   beta); any future energy-name add stacks both buckets. Not blocking at 6.00% NAV.
4. **Liquidity realism** — ADV IDR 79,771,692,717/day; 20% participation = IDR 15,954,338,543/day. Full 6.00%
   position (IDR 913,796,414) exits in **0.06 days** (≪ 7d). Liquidity cap 733% NAV — non-binding. PASS.
5. **Kill-criteria hygiene** — price  2027-09-30
   (review), kpi reserve_replacement_ratio < 1.0 (source AR2025 2P table p.75). All machine-monitorable with
   named sources. Note: kill 920 = -34.3% below entry 1,400 — a deep falsification level, not a near-term
   risk stop; the position has no tight loss bound by design.
6. **Sizing audit** — anchor `recommended_pct` = **10.0% NAV** (binding: constitution_cap; kelly_quarter
   21.48%, liquidity 733.29%). Judge PASS_REDUCED **0.60** binds → **PM cap 6.00% NAV**. PM has not sized; no
   breach. Sizer confirms "PM multiplies recommended_pct by 0.6 (= 6.00% NAV)".

Verdict: **CLEAR_WITH_NOTES** — both hard gates remediated, tags in taxonomy, liquidity and heat trivial;
notes are the double-factor-tag count and the -34.3% kill depth.
